title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Toyota 2000GT

scenes.text: Most people know the Toyota 2000GT as the Japanese car from a James Bond film. Far fewer know how it started, or what it cost the company that built it. Here are two things you probably did not know about the Toyota 2000GT, and along the way, every place where our sources disagree with each other.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE TOYOTA 2000GT

scenes.text: Our sources are Wikipedia's pages on the Toyota 2000GT, the Nissan S30 and the Nissan Z-car, Classic and Sports Car on the twenty twenty-two Gooding sale, Hagerty, Sports Car Market, Shannons Club and Luxury Entertainment Partners. Where they conflict, we show both versions. Our own arithmetic is always labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA (TOYOTA 2000GT, NISSAN S30, NISSAN Z) · CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR (MAR 2022) · HAGERTY · SPORTS CAR MARKET · SHANNONS CLUB · LEP · DISAGREEMENTS SHOWN

scenes.text: The first thing you probably did not know is that Toyota was not the first company offered this car. Wikipedia's page on the Nissan Z says Nissan partnered with Yamaha, which produced a prototype called the YX-30 in nineteen sixty-one. By nineteen sixty-four, the page says, Nissan had scrapped the project.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (NISSAN Z-CAR): NISSAN + YAMAHA → YX-30 PROTOTYPE, 1961 · BY 1964 NISSAN HAD SCRAPPED THE PROJECT
scenes.chapter: Thing one: Toyota was Nissan's second choice

scenes.text: The reason, according to that same page, was that Yamaha's twin-cam two litre engine did not meet Nissan's expectations. Yamaha then took the design to Toyota. The result, says Wikipedia, was the Toyota 2000GT. So the car that became Japan's first supercar began as a design that another Japanese carmaker had walked away from.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (NISSAN Z-CAR): YAMAHA'S DOHC 2.0 L ENGINE 'DID NOT MEET NISSAN'S EXPECTATIONS' · YAMAHA TOOK THE DESIGN TO TOYOTA → TOYOTA 2000GT

scenes.text: The story has a second layer. The Shannons Club article says Nissan hired a German aristocrat, Albrecht Goertz, as a consultant from May nineteen sixty-three. He built a Nissan prototype called the A550X, with many styling themes later seen on the Datsun 240Z. It says Goertz then moved to Toyota and developed the 2000GT.
scenes.caption: SHANNONS CLUB: ALBRECHT GOERTZ CONSULTED BY NISSAN FROM MAY 1963 · BUILT A550X PROTOTYPE WITH MANY 240Z STYLING THEMES · THEN MOVED TO TOYOTA AND DEVELOPED THE 2000GT

scenes.text: Our sources do not tell this story the same way. The Hagerty article says Yamaha's A550X concept was rejected by Nissan, and that Toyota also passed on it at first, but saw Yamaha as a possible partner, which led to the 2000GT. The Wikipedia page on the Toyota 2000GT does not mention Goertz at all in the passages we read.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: YAMAHA'S A550X REJECTED BY NISSAN; TOYOTA 'ALSO PASSED' BUT SAW YAMAHA AS A PARTNER → 2000GT · SHANNONS: GOERTZ MOVED TO TOYOTA · WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): NO GOERTZ MENTION IN WHAT WE READ

scenes.text: So there are three versions of the handover. In one, Nissan scrapped Yamaha's project, and Yamaha went to Toyota. In another, Goertz himself moved. In a third, Toyota first said no, then came back. They are not necessarily contradictory, but none of our sources explains how they fit together, and we will not guess at the order.
scenes.caption: VERSION 1: NISSAN SCRAPPED, YAMAHA → TOYOTA · VERSION 2: GOERTZ MOVED TO TOYOTA · VERSION 3: TOYOTA FIRST PASSED, THEN PARTNERED · HOW THEY FIT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: What the sources agree on is the outcome. Shannons says Toyota sold few 2000GTs but gained publicity, and that this pushed Nissan to take the Goertz prototype toward production. The Wikipedia page on the S30 says the same thing from the other side: the 2000GT's success prompted Nissan to continue developing its own sports car, which became the 240Z.
scenes.caption: SHANNONS: TOYOTA SOLD FEW BUT GAINED PUBLICITY → PUSHED NISSAN TO PRODUCE THE GOERTZ PROTOTYPE · HAGERTY: 2000GT'S SUCCESS PROMPTED NISSAN TO CONTINUE → 240Z
scenes.orig_query: A rival made by a rejection

scenes.text: The dates support that. Wikipedia says the Toyota 2000GT was shown at the Tokyo Motor Show in nineteen sixty-five, and production ran from May nineteen sixty-seven to August nineteen seventy. The Datsun 240Z was shown at the Tokyo Motor Show on the eighteenth of October nineteen sixty-nine, per Shannons. By our arithmetic, that is four years after the 2000GT's first appearance.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): TOKYO MOTOR SHOW 1965 · PRODUCTION MAY 1967 – AUG 1970 · SHANNONS: 240Z AT TOKYO MOTOR SHOW 18 OCT 1969 · 1965 → 1969 = 4 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: There is one more detail. Wikipedia says Yamaha, the motorcycle and engine maker, built the 2000GT cars at its factory at Iwata, in Shizuoka prefecture. So the car sold under a Toyota badge was assembled by a company better known for motorcycles, using a design that Nissan had dropped. That is the first thing most people do not know.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): YAMAHA BUILT THE CARS AT IWATA, SHIZUOKA · TOYOTA-BADGED · NISSAN HAD DROPPED THE DESIGN (WIKIPEDIA, NISSAN Z)

scenes.text: The second thing you probably did not know is that the car that made Toyota look like a serious sports car maker lost the company money. Wikipedia's page says that only about sixty cars reached North America, and that Toyota made no profit from the 2000GT. The car was a statement, not a business.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): ABOUT 60 CARS REACHED NORTH AMERICA · TOYOTA MADE NO PROFIT
scenes.chapter: Thing two: Toyota did not make money on it

scenes.text: The plan was far larger than the result. Classic and Sports Car, writing about the twenty twenty-two Gooding sale, says Toyota hoped to build a thousand cars a year, but in the end built three hundred fifty-one. Production ran for about three and a quarter years. By our arithmetic, a thousand a year over that time would have been about three thousand two hundred fifty cars.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR (MAR 2022): TOYOTA HOPED FOR 1,000 A YEAR, BUILT 351 · MAY 1967 – AUG 1970 ≈ 3.25 YEARS · 1,000 × 3.25 = ~3,250 (OUR ARITHMETIC)
scenes.orig_query: A plan for a thousand a year

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, three hundred fifty-one cars is about eleven percent of that hoped-for volume. Or put another way, one year of the original plan would have been nearly three times the entire production run. The sources do not say whether the thousand a year was a target on paper, or something Toyota actually tooled up for.
scenes.caption: 351 ÷ 3,250 = 10.8% · 1,000 ÷ 351 = 2.8× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WHETHER 1,000/YEAR WAS A FORMAL TARGET: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The count of cars is itself disputed. Wikipedia's infobox gives three hundred fifty-one, split into two hundred thirty-three MF10, one hundred nine MF10L and nine MF12L cars. But its text says three hundred thirty-seven regular production units. Sports Car Market says three hundred fifty-four were built. Neither page reconciles the figures.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT) INFOBOX: 233 MF10 + 109 MF10L + 9 MF12L = 351 · SAME PAGE TEXT: 337 'REGULAR' UNITS · SPORTS CAR MARKET: 354 BUILT · NO RECONCILIATION

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the spread between three hundred thirty-seven and three hundred fifty-four is seventeen cars, about five percent. The left-hand-drive count is also contested. Sports Car Market's table lists eighty-four left-hand-drive cars, while its text says sixty-two. Luxury Entertainment Partners also describes a car as one of sixty-two US-market cars.
scenes.caption: 354 − 337 = 17 (5.0%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SCM: 84 LHD IN TABLE vs 62 IN TEXT · LEP: 'ONE OF 62 US-MARKET CARS' · WIKIPEDIA: ~60 TO NORTH AMERICA

scenes.text: Why would a company make a car it could not sell at a profit? The price gives a clue. Wikipedia says the 2000GT cost about seven thousand one hundred fifty dollars in the United States in nineteen sixty-eight. Sports Car Market gives an original list price of six thousand eight hundred. We cannot tell which is right, or whether one is a base price and the other a delivered one.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): US PRICE 1968 ≈ $7,150 · SPORTS CAR MARKET: ORIGINAL LIST PRICE $6,800 · DIFFERENCE $350 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BASIS OF EACH FIGURE: NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: Wikipedia puts the 2000GT's price in context. In nineteen sixty-eight, a Jaguar E-Type cost five thousand five hundred thirty-nine dollars, a Porsche 911S six thousand seven hundred ninety, and a Ferrari 365 GTB/4 nineteen thousand seven hundred. By our arithmetic, the Toyota cost twenty-nine percent more than the Jaguar and five percent more than the Porsche.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT), 1968 US PRICES: 2000GT ~$7,150 · E-TYPE $5,539 · 911S $6,790 · FERRARI 365 GTB/4 $19,700 · 7,150 ÷ 5,539 = +29.1% · 7,150 ÷ 6,790 = +5.3% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Against the Ferrari, the picture is reversed. By our arithmetic, the 2000GT cost thirty-six percent of the Ferrari's price, so the Ferrari cost two point eight times as much. Toyota priced its car above the Jaguar and Porsche but well below Ferrari. The sources do not say how Toyota chose that price, or what each car cost to build.
scenes.caption: 7,150 ÷ 19,700 = 36.3% · 19,700 ÷ 7,150 = 2.8× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · TOYOTA'S PRICING LOGIC AND BUILD COST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: So the second thing most people do not know is the gap between the image and the books. The car looked like a triumph, and it later became one. But at the time, according to Wikipedia, Toyota earned nothing from it. The profit, if you want to call it that, came later, and it went to the people who owned the cars, not to Toyota.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): TOYOTA MADE NO PROFIT · LATER AUCTION GAINS WENT TO OWNERS (OUR READING OF THE AUCTION DATA THAT FOLLOWS)

scenes.text: To understand why anyone wanted it, look at the car. Wikipedia lists a length of four thousand one hundred seventy-five millimetres, a width of sixteen hundred, and a height of only eleven hundred sixty, with a two thousand three hundred thirty wheelbase. It weighed eleven hundred twenty kilograms.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): L 4,175 MM · W 1,600 MM · H 1,160 MM · WHEELBASE 2,330 MM · 1,120 KG · 1,160 MM = 45.7 IN (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The engine was a one thousand nine hundred eighty-eight cubic centimetre inline six, called the 3M. Wikipedia says it started from the block of the Toyota Crown's engine, with a twin-cam head developed by Yamaha and three two-barrel Mikuni-Solex carburettors. So even the engine was a collaboration, a Toyota block with a Yamaha head.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 1,988 CC 3M INLINE-SIX · CROWN S50 BLOCK · YAMAHA DOHC HEAD · THREE 2-BARREL MIKUNI-SOLEX CARBURETTORS

scenes.text: It made a hundred fifty metric horsepower at sixty-six hundred revs, which Wikipedia converts to one hundred forty-eight horsepower, and one hundred seventy-five newton-metres of torque at five thousand. Sports Car Market says one hundred fifty horsepower at seven thousand revs. By our arithmetic, that is about seventy-six metric horsepower per litre, and one hundred thirty-four per tonne.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 150 PS (148 HP) @ 6,600 RPM; 175 N·M @ 5,000 · SCM: 150 HP @ 7,000 RPM · 150 ÷ 1.988 = 75.5 PS/L · 150 ÷ 1.12 = 133.9 PS/TONNE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Wikipedia gives a claimed top speed of one hundred thirty-five miles an hour, and says it was a claim, with the figure tied to a particular axle ratio. It also claims thirty-one miles per gallon, and gives no zero to sixty time. Classic and Sports Car mentions an early development car, Project two eighty A, at a hundred forty-eight brake horsepower and one hundred thirty-seven miles an hour.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): TOP SPEED 135 MPH CLAIMED (4.375 AXLE) · FUEL ECONOMY 31 MPG CLAIMED · NO 0–60 TIME · CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: PROJECT 280A, 148 BHP, 137 MPH · LEP: 146 MPH, 150 BHP

scenes.text: The top speed itself is disputed. Wikipedia says one hundred thirty-five, Classic and Sports Car says one hundred thirty-seven for the prototype, and Luxury Entertainment Partners says one hundred forty-six. By our arithmetic, the spread is eleven miles an hour. None of the three says who measured it, so we treat them all as claims rather than test results.
scenes.caption: 135 vs 137 (PROTOTYPE) vs 146 MPH · 146 − 135 = 11 MPH (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WHO MEASURED: NOT STATED → CLAIMS, NOT TESTS

scenes.text: It was not only a show car. Wikipedia lists a third place at the nineteen sixty-six Japanese Grand Prix, a win at the nineteen sixty-six Suzuka one thousand kilometres, and wins in nineteen sixty-seven at the Fuji twenty-four hours and the Fuji one thousand kilometres. The car was entered in real races in its first seasons.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 1966 JAPANESE GP 3RD · 1966 SUZUKA 1000 KM WIN · 1967 24 HOURS OF FUJI WIN · 1967 FUJI 1000 KM WIN

scenes.text: Wikipedia also describes a speed-record attempt at Yatabe in nineteen sixty-six, saying the car broke thirteen records in seventy-two hours. Our sources do not give the individual records, the drivers, or the speeds, so we can report the headline only. The page uses the figure seventy-two, which is three days, and we have no other source to compare it with.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 1966 YATABE TEST — 13 RECORDS IN 72 HOURS · 72 H = 3 DAYS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · INDIVIDUAL RECORDS, DRIVERS, SPEEDS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · SINGLE-SOURCE CLAIM

scenes.text: The Shelby racing program is better documented. Classic and Sports Car says Carroll Shelby's team ran three Toyota-Shelby cars in the nineteen sixty-eight SCCA championship, with chassis numbers 10001, 10005 and 10006, driven by Dave Jordan and Scooter Patrick. It finished fourth in the National Championship, with four wins, eight seconds and six thirds.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: 3 TOYOTA-SHELBY CARS (MF10-10001, -10005, -10006) · DRIVERS DAVE JORDAN, SCOOTER PATRICK · 1968 SCCA NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP: 4TH · 4 WINS, 8 SECONDS, 6 THIRDS

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, four wins, eight seconds and six thirds make eighteen podium finishes in one season. Wikipedia adds that the Shelby cars ran in the SCCA's C Production class, and only for one season. Our sources do not say why the program ended after a year, so we leave that question open.
scenes.caption: 4 + 8 + 6 = 18 PODIUMS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: SCCA CP CLASS, 3 CARS, ONE SEASON · REASON IT ENDED: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Of course, the other reason people know the 2000GT is James Bond. Wikipedia says it appeared in You Only Live Twice in nineteen sixty-seven, and that two topless one-off cars were built for the film. The page notes that Daniel Craig has named it his favourite Bond car, a detail the page does not date.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): FEATURED IN YOU ONLY LIVE TWICE (1967) · TWO TOPLESS ONE-OFFS BUILT FOR THE FILM · DANIEL CRAIG'S FAVOURITE BOND CAR (UNDATED)

scenes.text: A note on what we cannot say. Our sources do not explain why the film cars were topless, how much they cost to build, or where they are today. Many articles online repeat stories about the filming, but we only found the single line on Wikipedia in the pages we read, so we leave the stories out. The Bond link is real, but thin in our sources.
scenes.caption: TOPLESS CONVERSION REASON, BUILD COST, CURRENT WHEREABOUTS OF FILM CARS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · ONLINE FILMING ANECDOTES NOT VERIFIED → OMITTED

scenes.text: Now the part that shows what the car became. Sports Car Market lists auction results for the 2000GT over three decades. In nineteen ninety-two, two cars failed to sell, with bids of sixty thousand and forty-two thousand five hundred dollars. In August nineteen ninety-eight, one sold for seventy-seven thousand five hundred. In March nineteen ninety-nine, another sold for sixty-nine thousand three hundred.
scenes.caption: SPORTS CAR MARKET: 1992 — TWO NO-SALES AT $60,000 AND $42,500 · AUG 1998 — $77,500 · MAR 1999 — $69,300

scenes.text: Then the prices climbed. Sports Car Market lists one hundred fifty-one thousand dollars in October two thousand, two hundred twenty-five thousand six hundred in July two thousand six, and six hundred twenty-seven thousand in August two thousand twelve. By our arithmetic, that is a rise from the March nineteen ninety-nine sale of nine times in thirteen years.
scenes.caption: SCM: OCT 2000 $151,000 · JUL 2006 $225,600 · AUG 2012 $627,000 · 627,000 ÷ 69,300 = 9.0× (MAR 1999 → AUG 2012, 13.4 YEARS) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: On the twenty-seventh of April twenty thirteen, at RM Auctions in Fort Worth, a car owned by Don Davis sold for one million one hundred fifty-five thousand dollars, according to Sports Car Market, a record for a Japanese car. By our arithmetic, that was eighty-four percent more than the August twenty twelve sale, eight months earlier.
scenes.caption: SCM: 27 APR 2013, RM FORT WORTH (DON DAVIS CAR) $1,155,000 — RECORD FOR A JAPANESE CAR · 1,155,000 ÷ 627,000 = +84.2% · AUG 2012 → APR 2013 = 8 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the million-dollar sale was more than fifteen times the nineteen ninety-eight price of seventy-seven thousand five hundred, in fifteen years. The sources do not say whether the same cars were sold repeatedly, so these are not returns on one car. They are a record of what different cars fetched at different sales.
scenes.caption: 1,155,000 ÷ 77,500 = 14.9× (AUG 1998 → APR 2013, ~14.7 YEARS) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SAME CAR RESOLD? NOT STATED → NOT A RETURN ON ONE CAR

scenes.text: The most recent big result in our sources is from the Gooding sale at Amelia Island on the fourth of March twenty twenty-two. Classic and Sports Car says the Toyota-Shelby car, chassis ten thousand one, sold for two million five hundred thirty-five thousand dollars. Its estimate was two point seven five to three point five million, so it sold below the low estimate.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: GOODING AMELIA ISLAND, 4 MAR 2022 · MF10-10001 SOLD $2,535,000 · ESTIMATE $2.75–3.5 M · BELOW LOW ESTIMATE

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that is eight percent below the low estimate, and two point two times the two thirteen Fort Worth price. Hagerty says it was a record for a Japanese car at auction, beating the one point seven five million paid for a nineteen eighty-nine Mazda 767B at Amelia in twenty seventeen. By our arithmetic, the Toyota was forty-five percent higher.
scenes.caption: 2.535 ÷ 2.75 = 92.2% (−7.8%) · 2,535,000 ÷ 1,155,000 = 2.2× · HAGERTY: RECORD FOR JAPANESE CAR AT AUCTION; PREVIOUS 1989 MAZDA 767B $1.75 M (AMELIA 2017) · 2.535 ÷ 1.75 = +44.9% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The records leapfrogged each other. Per Sports Car Market, a 2000GT set the Japanese-car record at one million one hundred fifty-five thousand in twenty thirteen. Hagerty says the Mazda 767B took it with one point seven five million in twenty seventeen. Then the Toyota-Shelby took it back in twenty twenty-two. By our arithmetic, the Mazda beat the 2013 record by fifty-two percent.
scenes.caption: 2013: 2000GT $1,155,000 (SCM) → 2017: MAZDA 767B $1.75 M (HAGERTY) → 2022: TOYOTA-SHELBY $2.535 M · 1.75 ÷ 1.155 = +51.5% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: One more number from Classic and Sports Car. It says the 2000GT holds the top eighteen Toyota auction prices, and that two other nineteen sixty-seven cars sold at that sale for one million one hundred fifty-five thousand dollars each. By our arithmetic, there is no other Toyota model among the eighteen most expensive Toyotas ever sold at auction, according to that source.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: 2000GTs HOLD THE TOP 18 TOYOTA AUCTION PRICES · TWO OTHER 1967 CARS SOLD $1,155,000 EACH AT THAT SALE · CLAIM IS THE MAGAZINE'S, NOT INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED

scenes.text: The Datsun 240Z arrived because of the 2000GT, as we saw. Wikipedia says the American version was released on the twenty-second of October nineteen sixty-nine, with a two point four litre inline six making one hundred fifty-one horsepower on the old SAE gross measure. The 2000GT's one hundred forty-eight horsepower is a different measurement, so the two numbers are not directly comparable.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (NISSAN S30): US 240Z RELEASED 22 OCT 1969 · 2.4 L L24 I6 · 151 HP SAE GROSS · 2000GT 150 PS = 148 HP (WIKIPEDIA) · DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT BASES → NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE

scenes.text: The sales gap is enormous. Wikipedia's page on the S30 says over forty-five thousand 240Zs were sold in the United States through the nineteen seventy-one model year, over fifty thousand in nineteen seventy-two and forty thousand in nineteen seventy-three. By our arithmetic, that is at least one hundred thirty-five thousand cars in about four years, against three hundred fifty-one 2000GTs.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (NISSAN S30): US 240Z — 45,000+ THRU MY1971 · 50,000+ 1972 · 40,000 1973 · 45 + 50 + 40 = 135 THOUSAND MINIMUM · 135,000 ÷ 351 = 385× (OUR ARITHMETIC; 'OVER' MEANS TRUE FIGURE IS HIGHER)

scenes.text: Shannons Club says the 240Z offered about ninety percent of the Jaguar E-Type's performance and appeal for little more than half the price, and became the best-selling sports car in the world. That is the opposite business from Toyota's. One company chased prestige at a loss, and the other chased volume with a car priced to sell.
scenes.caption: SHANNONS CLUB: 240Z ≈ 90% OF E-TYPE PERFORMANCE AND APPEAL FOR 'LITTLE MORE THAN HALF THE PRICE' · 'WORLD'S BEST-SELLING SPORTS CAR' · 240Z US LAUNCH PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Hagerty adds a final twist. It says the 240Z changed how the world saw Japanese carmakers, from makers of curious cars to world-class automakers. That is Hagerty's opinion, not a measurement. But if it is right, the 2000GT's role was to open the door, and the Datsun walked through it with far more cars.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: 240Z MOVED JAPANESE CARMAKERS 'FROM MANUFACTURERS OF CURIOUS CARS TO WORLD-CLASS AUTOMAKERS' (OPINION, NOT A MEASUREMENT) · 'DOOR-OPENER' = OUR READING

scenes.text: Nissan answered the 2000GT in Japan with a car most people never saw. Hagerty describes the Fairlady Z432, which used the twin-cam S20 racing engine from the Skyline GT-R, cost twice as much as the base Z in Japan, and sold poorly. Wikipedia puts production of the Z432 at about four hundred twenty, and the even rarer Z432R at under fifty.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: Z432 USED THE DOHC S20 ENGINE; TWICE THE PRICE OF BASE Z IN JAPAN; SOLD POORLY · WIKIPEDIA (S30): Z432 ~420 BUILT; Z432R UNDER 50

scenes.text: One Z432R sold for one point one seven million Australian dollars in January twenty twenty, about eight hundred thirty-seven thousand US dollars, according to Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, the Toyota-Shelby sale was three times that figure. So the same story repeats: a rare Japanese car with racing hardware, ignored when new, and expensive decades later.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (S30): Z432R SOLD A$1.17 M (≈ US$837K) JAN 2020 · 2,535 ÷ 837 = 3.0× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'IGNORED WHEN NEW' APPLIES TO Z432 PER HAGERTY ('SOLD POORLY'), NOT SPECIFIC TO THE Z432R

scenes.text: Classic and Sports Car gives the history of the car sold in twenty twenty-two. Chassis ten thousand one was the first serial-numbered Toyota-Shelby, built on the twenty-seventh of September nineteen sixty-six in Solar Red. It was one of three Shelby-run cars, and the magazine says Project two eighty A had started in the summer of nineteen sixty-four.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: MF10-10001 FIRST SERIAL-NUMBERED CAR, BUILT 27 SEP 1966, SOLAR RED · PROJECT 280A STARTED SUMMER 1964 · 1964 → 1966 ≈ 2 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Luxury Entertainment Partners listed chassis one hundred, a left-hand-drive car in Solar Red, at nine hundred twelve thousand five hundred dollars, about six hundred ninety-six thousand pounds. The listing calls it a nineteen seventy-six model year. But Wikipedia says production ended in August nineteen seventy. That is a conflict we cannot resolve, and it may be a listing error.
scenes.caption: LEP: CHASSIS 100, LHD, SOLAR RED, $912,500 (≈ £696K) · LISTING SAYS '1976 MODEL YEAR' · WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): PRODUCTION ENDED AUG 1970 → CONFLICT, UNRESOLVED (POSSIBLE LISTING ERROR — OUR GUESS)

scenes.text: The same listing says the car took part in rallies, including the Copperstate one thousand in twenty ten, and names owners Otto Linton and Brown Maloney. By our arithmetic, this car at nine hundred twelve thousand dollars was about a quarter below the Fort Worth record, so the market for the ordinary cars sits between the headline prices.
scenes.caption: LEP: OWNER HISTORY OTTO LINTON, BROWN MALONEY; 2010 COPPERSTATE 1000 RALLY · 912,500 ÷ 1,155,000 = 79% (−21%) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · LISTING PRICE = ASKING, NOT A SALE

scenes.text: Classic and Sports Car adds context on the Gooding sale. Of ninety-nine lots offered, ninety-three sold for a total of sixty-nine million two hundred nine thousand four hundred eighty dollars. By our arithmetic, the Toyota-Shelby alone was almost four percent of the entire sale, and the average lot made about seven hundred forty-four thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR: 99 LOTS, 93 SOLD, $69,209,480 · 2,535,000 ÷ 69,209,480 = 3.7% · 69,209,480 ÷ 93 = $744,187 AVERAGE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: A last number about expectations. Sports Car Market quotes a dealer, Braden, saying in two thousand one that good cars would stay around one hundred thousand to one hundred fifty thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, the two thirteen record was seven point seven times the top of that range. Predictions about collectible cars often fail, and this one did.
scenes.caption: SCM: BRADEN, 2001 — GOOD CARS WOULD STAY AT $100,000–150,000 · 1,155,000 ÷ 150,000 = 7.7× · ÷ 100,000 = 11.6× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'PREDICTIONS OFTEN FAIL' = OUR COMMENT

scenes.text: Here is what we could not confirm. We have no verified figure for what the 2000GT cost Toyota to build, so the claim of no profit rests on one line of Wikipedia. We have no official total of cars sold in each country. We have no independent test of the top speed, and no zero to sixty time. And the Goertz story is told three ways.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: BUILD COST / LOSS PER CAR · UNITS PER COUNTRY · INDEPENDENT TOP-SPEED OR 0–60 TEST · HOW THE GOERTZ / NISSAN / TOYOTA HANDOVER FIT TOGETHER · 'NO PROFIT' = ONE WIKIPEDIA LINE
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: So the two things, again. First, the 2000GT began as a design another Japanese carmaker dropped, and it ended up in Toyota's hands through Yamaha. Second, Toyota built three hundred fifty-one of them against a hope of a thousand a year, and made no profit. Everything else, the racing, the Bond film, the auction records, came afterwards.
scenes.caption: 1) A DESIGN NISSAN DROPPED → YAMAHA → TOYOTA · 2) 351 BUILT vs HOPED 1,000 A YEAR · NO PROFIT · THE FAME AND AUCTION PRICES CAME LATER

scenes.text: If you want to go deeper, the next video compares the 2000GT with the Datsun 240Z, the car it indirectly inspired. All sources are in the description. If this was useful, subscribe to Pickup Reality, and tell us which exotic car you want us to check next.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
